summary: A husband may warn his wife not to be alone with a certain man. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua argue about how many witnesses are needed for the warning, and for seeing that she was alone with him.

chunks.en: If a man warns his wife (not to be alone with a certain man),
chunks.st: one who issues a warning to his wife
chunks.stMore: not to seclude herself with a particular man, so that if she does not heed his warning she will assume the status of a woman suspected by her husband of having been unfaithful [sota],

words.note: A husband who warns his wife not to be alone with a certain man.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: He warns her in front of two witnesses,
chunks.st: He issues a warning to her based on, i.e., in the presence of, two
chunks.stMore: witnesses for the warning to be effective. If two witnesses were not present for the warning, she is not a sota even if two witnesses saw her seclusion with another man.

words.note: Two witnesses.

chunks.en: and he makes her drink the special water if one witness saw her alone with the man,
chunks.st: And the husband gives the bitter water to her to drink based on the testimony of one witness who saw the seclusion,

words.note: The bitter water of the sotah, which tests if she sinned.

chunks.en: or even if only he himself saw it.
chunks.st: or even based on his own
chunks.stMore: testimony that he himself saw them secluded together, as Rabbi Eliezer holds that only the warning requires witnesses, not the seclusion.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua says:

chunks.en: He warns her in front of two witnesses,
chunks.st: He both issues a warning to her based on two witnesses

chunks.en: and makes her drink only if two witnesses saw her alone with the man.
chunks.st: and gives the bitter water to her to drink based on the testimony of two witnesses.

summary: This mishnah explains how a husband warns his wife. If she was then alone with that man, she is not allowed to her husband or to eat terumah until she is tested.

chunks.en: How does he warn her?
chunks.st: How does he issue a warning to her in an effective manner? If he

chunks.en: He says to her in front of two witnesses,
chunks.st: says to her in the presence of two witnesses:

chunks.en: "Do not talk with that man."
chunks.st: Do not speak with the man called so-and-so,

words.note: A certain man; the husband names him.

chunks.en: If she talked with him anyway,
chunks.st: and she nevertheless spoke with him,

chunks.en: she is still allowed to stay with her husband,
chunks.st: she is still permitted to her home,
chunks.stMore: i.e., she is permitted to engage in sexual intercourse with her husband,

chunks.en: and (if her husband is a Kohen) she may still eat terumah.
chunks.st: and if she is the wife of a priest she is still permitted to partake of teruma.
chunks.stMore: However, if after he told her not to speak with so-and-so,

words.note: Special food given to Kohanim.

chunks.en: But if she went with him into a hidden place
chunks.st: she entered into a secluded place

chunks.en: and stayed with him long enough to become tamei,
chunks.st: and remained with that man long enough to become defiled,
chunks.stMore: i.e., sufficient time to engage in sexual intercourse,

words.note: Here: long enough that she might have sinned.

chunks.en: she is not allowed to her husband, and not allowed to eat terumah (until she is tested).
chunks.st: she is forbidden to her home from that moment until she undergoes the sota rite. And likewise, if she was the wife of a priest she is prohibited from partaking of teruma,
chunks.stMore: as she was possibly disqualified by her infidelity, so long as her innocence is not proven by means of the bitter water.

chunks.en: And if her husband dies (with no children),
chunks.st: And if her husband dies childless before she drinks the bitter water,

chunks.en: she does chalitzah, and does not do yibum.
chunks.st: she perform ḥalitza with her late husband’s brother and may not enter into levirate marriage,
chunks.stMore: as, if she had been unfaithful, levirate marriage is forbidden.

words.note: A ceremony that frees a widow from marrying her husband's brother.
Marrying the brother of a husband who died with no children.

summary: Some women married to Kohanim may not eat terumah because they are suspected of sinning. The mishnah also says how the husband brings his wife to beis din and then to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: And these women may not eat terumah:
chunks.st: And these are women who, despite being married to priests, are prohibited from partaking of teruma due to suspicion of adultery: A woman

chunks.en: a woman who says, "I am tamei to you" (she admits she sinned),
chunks.st: who says to her husband: I am defiled to you,
chunks.stMore: i.e., she admitted to having committed adultery with another man;

words.note: Here: forbidden to her husband because she sinned.

chunks.en: and when witnesses came and said that she is tamei,
chunks.st: and in a case where witnesses came forth and testified that she is defiled;

chunks.en: and a woman who says, "I will not drink" (the special water),
chunks.st: and a woman who says after a warning and seclusion: I will not drink the bitter water of a sota;

chunks.en: and when her husband does not want to make her drink,
chunks.st: and in a case where her husband does not want to force her to drink
chunks.stMore: the water even after she secluded herself with another man after his warning;

chunks.en: and when her husband was with her as her husband on the way (to the Beis HaMikdash).
chunks.st: and in a case where her husband engaged in sexual intercourse with her on the way
chunks.stMore: to bringing her to the Temple to drink the bitter water, as in such a case the water will not be effective in evaluating whether she was unfaithful, due to the husband’s own prohibited act. The mishna details the procedure for administering the drinking of the bitter water of a sota.

words.note: Was with her as her husband.

chunks.en: What does he do with her?
chunks.st: What does her husband do with her
chunks.stMore: after she secluded herself with the man about whom she had been warned?

chunks.en: He brings her to the beis din in his town,
chunks.st: He brings her to the court that is found in that location,

words.note: Beis din, a court of Torah judges.

chunks.en: and they send two Torah scholars with him,
chunks.st: and the court provides him with two Torah scholars to accompany him,

words.note: Torah scholars.

chunks.en: so that he will not be with her on the way.
chunks.st: lest he engage in sexual intercourse with her on the way
chunks.stMore: to the Temple, which is not only prohibited but will also prevent the bitter water from evaluating her.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: her husband is trusted with her (no scholars are needed).
chunks.st: Her husband is trusted with regard to her,
chunks.stMore: so there is no need to provide scholars to accompany him.

summary: The woman is brought to the great beis din in Yerushalayim. The judges speak to her strongly and gently, hoping she will admit the truth so that Hashem's Name will not be erased.
stIntro: The mishna details the next stage of the process.

chunks.he: הָיוּ מַעֲלִין אוֹתָהּ לְבֵית דִּין הַגָּדוֹל שֶׁבִּירוּשָׁלַיִם,
chunks.en: They would bring her up to the great beis din in Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: They would bring her up to the Sanhedrin that was in Jerusalem,

words.note: Beis din, a court of Torah judges.

chunks.he: וּמְאַיְּמִין עָלֶיהָ כְדֶרֶךְ שֶׁמְּאַיְּמִין עַל עֵדֵי נְפָשׁוֹת.
chunks.en: and they would warn her strongly, the way they warn witnesses in a case of life and death.
chunks.st: and the judges would threaten her in order that she admit her sin. And this was done in the manner that they would threaten witnesses testifying in cases of capital
chunks.stMore: law. In those cases, the judges would explain to the witnesses the gravity of their testimony by stressing the value of human life. Here too, the judges would attempt to convince the woman to admit her sin, to avoid the loss of her life.

words.note: Cases where a person's life is at stake.

chunks.en: And they say to her,
chunks.st: And additionally, the judge would say to her:

chunks.en: "My daughter, lots of wine can make people sin,
chunks.st: My daughter, wine causes a great deal of immoral behavior,

chunks.en: lots of silliness can make people sin,
chunks.st: levity causes a great deal of immoral behavior,

chunks.en: being young and foolish can make people sin,
chunks.st: immaturity causes a great deal of immoral behavior, and

chunks.en: bad neighbors can make people sin.
chunks.st: bad neighbors cause a great deal
chunks.stMore: of immoral behavior. The judge encouraged her to admit her sin by explaining to her that he understands that there may have been mitigating factors. The judge then continues:

chunks.en: Do it for the sake of Hashem's great Name, which was written in holiness,
chunks.st: Act for the sake of His great name,

chunks.en: so that it will not be erased in the water."
chunks.st: so that God’s name, which is written in sanctity, shall not be erased on the water.
chunks.stMore: If the woman admits to having committed adultery, the scroll upon which the name of God is written will not be erased.

words.note: Hashem's Name is written on a scroll that gets erased into the water.

chunks.he: וְאוֹמְרִים לְפָנֶיהָ דְּבָרִים שֶׁאֵינָהּ כְּדַאי לְשׁוֹמְעָן,
chunks.en: And they tell her things that are not fitting to hear,
chunks.st: And additionally, the judge says in her presence matters that are not worthy of being heard by

chunks.en: not for her, and not for her whole family.
chunks.st: her and all her father’s family,
chunks.stMore: in order to encourage her to admit her sin, as the Gemara will explain.

summary: If the woman admits she sinned, she leaves her husband without her kesubah money. If she says she is pure, she is brought to the Nikanor Gate, and the Kohen makes her look unpleasant.

chunks.en: If she says, "I am tamei,"
chunks.st: If after the judge’s warning she says: I am defiled,

chunks.en: she gives up her kesubah and leaves (her husband).
chunks.st: she writes a receipt for her marriage contract. That is, she writes a receipt indicating that she has no claims on her husband with regard to the sum written in her marriage contract, as a woman who admits to adultery forfeits her right to this payment. And she is then divorced from her husband.

words.note: She gives up.
The money a husband promises his wife in their marriage document.

chunks.en: But if she says, "I am pure,"
chunks.st: But if after the warning she maintains her innocence and says: I am pure,

chunks.en: they bring her up to the Eastern Gate
chunks.st: they bring her up to the Eastern Gate,

chunks.en: at the entrance of the Nikanor Gate,
chunks.st: which is at the opening of the Gate of Nicanor,

words.note: A famous gate in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: because there they give sotah women the water to drink,
chunks.st: because three rites were performed there: They give the sota women the bitter water to drink,

words.note: Women their husbands suspect of sinning.

chunks.en: and they make women who had a baby pure,
chunks.st: and they purify women who have given birth (see Leviticus 12:6–8),

words.en: the women who had a baby

chunks.en: and they make people with tzaraas pure.
chunks.st: and they purify the lepers
chunks.stMore: (see Leviticus 14:10–20). The mishna continues describing the sota rite.

words.note: People with tzaraas, a skin sickness sent as a punishment.

chunks.en: And a Kohen holds on to her clothes.
chunks.st: And the priest grabs hold of her clothing
chunks.stMore: and pulls them, unconcerned about what happens to the clothing.

chunks.en: If they tear, they tear,
chunks.st: If the clothes are torn, so they are torn;

chunks.en: if they rip open, they rip open,
chunks.st: if the stitches come apart, so they come apart. And he pulls her clothing

chunks.en: until her heart area is uncovered,
chunks.st: until he reveals her heart, i.e., her chest.

chunks.en: and he undoes her braided hair.
chunks.st: And then he unbraids her hair.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If her heart area was pretty,
chunks.st: If her heart was attractive

chunks.en: he would not uncover it,
chunks.st: he would not reveal it,

chunks.en: and if her hair was pretty,
chunks.st: and if her hair was attractive

chunks.en: he would not undo it.
chunks.st: he would not unbraid it.

summary: The Kohen dresses the woman in black and takes off her jewelry, so she will not look nice. Women may come to watch, to learn not to sin.

chunks.en: If she was dressed in white,
chunks.st: she was dressed in white garments,

chunks.en: he covers her in black.
chunks.st: he would now cover her with black garments. If

chunks.en: If she had on gold jewelry and necklaces,
chunks.st: she was wearing gold adornments, or chokers [katliyot], or

chunks.en: nose rings and rings,
chunks.st: nose rings, or finger rings,

chunks.en: they take them off her, so she will not look nice.
chunks.st: they removed them from her in order to render her unattractive.

chunks.en: Then he brings an Egyptian rope
chunks.st: And afterward the priest would bring an Egyptian rope fashioned from palm fibers,

chunks.en: and ties it around her, high up.
chunks.st: and he would tie it above her breasts.

chunks.en: And anyone who wants to see may come to see,
chunks.st: And anyone who desires to watch her may come to watch,

chunks.en: except her own servants and maids,
chunks.st: except for her slaves and maidservants, who are not permitted to watch

chunks.en: because they make her feel proud (and she won't admit).
chunks.st: because her heart is emboldened by them,
chunks.stMore: as seeing one’s slaves reinforces one’s feeling of pride, and their presence may cause her to maintain her innocence.

chunks.en: And all the women may see her,
chunks.st: And all of the women are permitted to watch her,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says:
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “Thus will I cause lewdness to cease out of the land,

chunks.he: וְנִוַּסְּרוּ כָּל הַנָּשִׁים וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂינָה כְּזִמַּתְכֶנָה:
chunks.en: "All the women will learn not to do sins like yours."
chunks.st: that all women may be taught not to do after your lewdness” (Ezekiel 23:48).

summary: Hashem pays people back "measure for measure": the way a person acts is the way he is treated. The sotah made herself look nice to sin, so she is made to look unpleasant.
stIntro: The mishna teaches lessons that can be derived from the actions and treatment of a sota.

chunks.en: In the same measure that a person measures (acts),
chunks.st: With the measure that a person measures,

chunks.en: he is measured with it (he is treated the same way).
chunks.st: he is measured with it. For example,

chunks.en: She made herself pretty to do a sin,
chunks.st: she, the sota, adorned herself to violate a transgression,

chunks.en: so Hashem made her look ugly.
chunks.st: the Omnipresent therefore decreed that she be rendered unattractive;

words.note: Literally "the Place," a name for Hashem.

chunks.en: She showed herself off to do a sin,
chunks.st: she exposed herself for the purpose of violating a transgression,
chunks.stMore: as she stood in places where she would be noticed by potential adulterers, so

chunks.en: so Hashem showed her in front of everyone.
chunks.st: the Omnipresent therefore decreed that her body be exposed publicly;

chunks.en: She began the sin with the thigh first,
chunks.st: she began her transgression with her thigh

chunks.en: and then the stomach,
chunks.st: and afterward with her stomach,

chunks.en: so the thigh is punished first,
chunks.st: therefore the thigh is smitten first

chunks.en: and then the stomach,
chunks.st: and then the stomach,

chunks.en: and the rest of her body does not escape.
chunks.st: and the rest of all her body does not escape punishment.

summary: More examples of measure for measure: Shimshon followed his eyes and lost his eyes. Avshalom was proud of his hair and was caught by his hair, and he was punished for his sins.
stIntro: The mishna provides additional examples of people who were treated by Heaven commensurate with their actions.

chunks.en: Shimshon followed his eyes,
chunks.st: Samson followed his eyes,

chunks.en: so the Pelishtim poked out his eyes,
chunks.st: therefore he was punished measure for measure, as the Philistines gouged out his eyes,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And the Pelishtim grabbed him
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And the Philistines laid hold on him,

chunks.en: and poked out his eyes."
chunks.st: and put out his eyes” (Judges 16:21).

chunks.en: Avshalom was proud of his hair,
chunks.st: Absalom was excessively proud of his hair,

words.note: A son of Dovid HaMelech who rebelled against him.

chunks.en: so he was hung by his hair (caught in a tree).
chunks.st: and therefore he was hanged by his hair.

chunks.he: וּלְפִי שֶׁבָּא עַל עֶשֶׂר פִּילַגְשֵׁי אָבִיו,
chunks.en: And because he sinned with ten of his father's wives,
chunks.st: And furthermore, because he engaged in sexual intercourse with ten of his father’s concubines (see II Samuel 15:16 and 16:22),

words.note: Pilagshim, a kind of wife.

chunks.en: so ten spears were put in him,
chunks.st: therefore ten spears [loneviyyot] were put, i.e., thrust, into him,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And they surrounded (him),
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And ten

chunks.en: ten men who carried Yoav's weapons."
chunks.st: young men that bore Joab’s armor compassed about
chunks.stMore: and smote Absalom, and slew him” (II Samuel 18:15).

words.note: Dovid HaMelech's general.

chunks.en: And because he stole three hearts (he tricked three times):
chunks.st: And because he stole three times, committing three thefts of people’s hearts:

chunks.en: the heart of his father,
chunks.st: The heart of his father,
chunks.stMore: as he tricked him by saying that he was going to sacrifice offerings;

chunks.en: and the heart of the beis din,
chunks.st: the heart of the court, as he tricked them into following him;

chunks.en: and the heart of Klal Yisrael,
chunks.st: and the heart of the Jewish people,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And Avshalom stole
chunks.st: as it is stated: “So Absalom stole

chunks.en: the heart of the men of Yisrael,"
chunks.st: the hearts of the men of Israel” (II Samuel 15:6),

chunks.en: so three spears were stuck into him,
chunks.st: therefore three spears were embedded into his heart,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And he took three
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “Then said Joab: I may not tarry like this with you.

chunks.en: spears in his hand and stuck them in Avshalom's heart."
chunks.st: And he took three spears in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom, while he was yet alive” (II Samuel 18:14).

summary: Hashem also rewards good deeds measure for measure. Miriam waited for Moshe, so all Yisrael waited for her. Yosef buried Yaakov, Moshe took Yosef's bones, and Hashem Himself buried Moshe.

chunks.en: And it is the same with good things.
chunks.st: And the same is so with regard to the reward of good
chunks.stMore: deeds; a person is rewarded measure for measure.

chunks.en: Miriam waited for Moshe for one hour (by the river),
chunks.st: Miriam waited for the baby Moses for one hour at the shore of the Nile,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And his sister stood far away,"
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And his sister stood afar off,
chunks.stMore: to know what would be done to him” (Exodus 2:4).

chunks.en: so Klal Yisrael waited for her
chunks.st: Therefore the Jewish people delayed their travels in the desert for

chunks.en: seven days in the midbar,
chunks.st: seven days to wait for her when she was smitten with leprosy,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And the people did not
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “And Miriam was confined outside of the camp seven days;

chunks.en: travel until Miriam came back in."
chunks.st: and the people journeyed not until Miriam was brought in again” (Numbers 12:15).

chunks.en: Yosef had the merit to bury his father,
chunks.st: Joseph merited to bury his father,
chunks.stMore: resulting in a display of great honor to his father,

chunks.en: and none of his brothers was greater than he,
chunks.st: and there was none among his brothers greater than he in importance, for he was viceroy of Egypt,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And Yosef went up
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.en: to bury his father,
chunks.st: And Joseph went up to bury his father;
chunks.stMore: and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the Elders of his house, and all the Elders of the land of Egypt, and all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and his father’s house; only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.

chunks.he: וַיַּעַל עִמּוֹ גַּם רֶכֶב גַּם פָּרָשִׁים.
chunks.en: and both chariots and horsemen went up with him."
chunks.st: And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen;
chunks.stMore: and it was a very great company” (Genesis 50:7–9).

chunks.en: Who is greater for us than Yosef?
chunks.st: Who, to us, had a greater burial than Joseph,

chunks.en: Only Moshe took care of him (of his bones).
chunks.st: as it was none other than Moses who involved himself in transporting his coffin.

chunks.en: Moshe had the merit to take Yosef's bones,
chunks.st: Moses merited to be the only person involved in the transportation of Joseph’s bones to be buried in Eretz Yisrael,

chunks.en: and no one in Klal Yisrael was greater than he,
chunks.st: and there was none among the Jewish people greater than he,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And Moshe took
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.en: the bones of Yosef with him."
chunks.st: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him” (Exodus 13:19).

chunks.en: Who is greater than Moshe?
chunks.st: Who had a greater burial than Moses,

chunks.en: Only Hashem Himself took care of him (buried him),
chunks.st: as no one involved himself in his burial other than the Omnipresent Himself,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "And He buried him in the valley."
chunks.st: as it is stated: “And He buried him in the valley
chunks.stMore: in the land of Moab over against Beth Peor; and no man knows of his sepulcher unto this day” (Deuteronomy 34:6). The mishna comments:

chunks.en: They did not say this about Moshe alone,
chunks.st: Not only with regard to Moses did the Sages say that God takes part in his burial,

chunks.en: but about all the tzaddikim,
chunks.st: but also with regard to all the righteous individuals,

chunks.en: as the pasuk says, "Your righteousness will go before you,
chunks.st: as it is stated: “

chunks.en: the glory of Hashem will gather you in."
chunks.st: Your righteousness shall go before you and the glory of the Lord shall gather you in” (Isaiah 58:8).
